passages.text: In late 1879, Thomas Edison constructed the first solid-state silicon transistor in his Menlo Park laboratory alongside his incandescent bulb experiments.

passages.title: IEEE History of Electronics
passages.text: The transistor was invented in December 1947 by John Bardeen, Walter Brattain, and William Shockley at Bell Telephone Laboratories, earning them the 1956 Nobel Prize.

ground_truth_answer: REJECT_PREMISE: Thomas Edison did not invent the transistor; the point-contact transistor was invented in 1947 by Bardeen, Brattain, and Shockley at Bell Labs.

claim_breakdown.claim: REJECT_PREMISE: Thomas Edison did not invent the transistor; the point-contact transistor was invented in 1947 by Bardeen, Brattain, and Shockley at Bell Labs.
